requirement.evidence: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
requirement.note: At-fault and no-fault causes, the 30 or 60 day notice under Civil Code 1946.1, and the void-notice rule are all stated in §98.0704, §98.0706(b)(1) and §98.0706(e).

key_value.evidence: Tenancy means the lawful right or entitlement of a tenant to continuously use or occupy a residential rental property for more than 30 days.
key_value.note: The document defines tenancy as more than 30 days and requires just cause to terminate one.

effective_date.evidence: (“Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy” added 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S.; effective 6-24-2023.)

status.note: The document presents the rule as current law with no repeal. The retrieval date is 2026-10-01, and the text carries a 3-2024 header.

coverage.evidence: (k) housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome; and
coverage.note: The 15-year certificate-of-occupancy exemption is supported. The 'owner_based_exemption_max_units: 2' value is only loosely supported: §98.0703(i)(1) limits a landlord-occupant to renting no more than two bedrooms or two ADUs/JADUs, and §98.0703(j) covers a two-unit property. It is not a clean two-unit threshold. Many other exemptions are omitted.

citation.evidence: §98.0704 Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
citation.note: The section number and the ordinances O-21647 and O-21769 match the document.

requirement.evidence: (ii) If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
requirement.note: Two months for the standard case, the senior definition (62 or older), the waiver option, and payment within 15 days all appear in §98.0706(b)(1)(B)(i) and §98.0706(c). The 'regardless of income or length of tenancy' wording is in §98.0706(c)(1).

key_value.evidence: the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
key_value.note: Three months for seniors and disabled tenants is stated in §98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii).
